implemented_requirements.requirement: All seven standard Tetromino shapes are present
Tetrominoes fall from the top of the board
implemented_requirements.evidence: self.spawn() sets self.py = 0 and the loop calls tick() which moves the piece down with self.py += 1 unless collide() is true.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can move pieces left and right
implemented_requirements.evidence: root.bind('<Left>', lambda e: self.move(-1)) and root.bind('<Right>', lambda e: self.move(1)) with move() checking collide() before updating self.px.
root.bind('<Up>', lambda e: self.rotate()) and rotate() creates a rotated matrix r and applies it if no collision.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Soft drop (down arrow) and hard drop (space) are supported
implemented_requirements.evidence: soft_drop() bound to '<Down>' and hard_drop() bound to '<space>' implement incremental and instant dropping.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Completed lines are cleared and board is updated
implemented_requirements.evidence: clear_lines() removes full rows, inserts empty rows at the top, updates self.lines and self.grid.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Scoring increases with line clears and drops
implemented_requirements.evidence: self.score is increased in clear_lines() using a table, in soft_drop() (+1 per cell) and hard_drop() (+2 per cell).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when a new piece cannot be placed
implemented_requirements.evidence: spawn() checks collide() at the top; if true, self.over = True and the loop stops.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board is redrawn after every move or drop
implemented_requirements.evidence: draw() is called at the end of move(), rotate(), soft_drop(), hard_drop(), tick(), lock(), toggle_pause() and when the game is over.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Drop speed increases as the game progresses
implemented_requirements.evidence: speed() returns max(90, 600 - (self.level-1)*55); level is increased in clear_lines() and self.delay is updated accordingly.

judge.summary: The provided main.py implements a complete, functional Tetris game using Tkinter. All seven tetromino shapes are defined, pieces fall, can be moved, rotated, soft‑ and hard‑dropped, lines are cleared, scoring and level progression are handled, and the drop speed accelerates with level. Game‑over detection and board redraws are present. The code appears syntactically correct and should run on a standard Python installation with Tkinter, giving a high likelihood of successful execution.
